title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to evaluate whether constrained prompting plus deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback (generate→verify→repair, one allowed repair) improves deterministic-verifier semantic correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic, verifier-capable intents spanning reachability/isolation, ACL-like access, VLAN/MTU sequences, and uplink switchover patterns; model = gpt-5-mini; execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Each intent produced one initial generation shared across baseline and guarded conditions; the guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call. Results: baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Only one guarded repair was applied (model_calls_used = 151; repair invocations = 1). Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow yielded a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over an already near-ceiling baseline. We emphasize methodological lessons for preregistered NetOps trials (baseline calibration, explicit generation semantics, and preregistered repair budgets). All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle referenced in the manifest.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces for network operations promise to reduce operator burden by letting administrators express desired configuration changes in free text that are automatically translated into executable device commands. Prior work documents that single-pass LLM outputs can contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that may cause unsafe or unavailable network states if applied directly [1],[2],[3]. A commonly proposed defensive architecture is a generate→verify→repair pipeline: an LLM produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants (or invariants derived from a formal spec), and an automated repair or human gate corrects violations before execution [4],[5]. Security analyses of tool-augmented LLM agents further motivate deterministic gating because unchecked textual claims can be converted into harmful actions in multi-tool workflows [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? The trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) was preregistered and frozen prior to any model interactions.
sections.related_work:
Three strands of prior literature frame this study. First, intent-to-configuration research finds modest semantic-correctness for free-text translation tasks and argues for post-generation checks to reduce unsafe outputs [1],[2]. Second, generate→verify→repair architectures (ranging from verifier-in-the-loop fine-tuning to policy-guided feedback) demonstrate correctness gains in infrastructure-as-code and configuration repair settings, but gains depend strongly on baseline model competence, repair budget, and sampling semantics [4],[7]. Third, security and systems analyses document claim-to-action vulnerabilities where LLM outputs combined with tooling can produce harmful actions, motivating auditable gating and verifier-aware planning [6],[8].

How this study situates. Our trial operationalizes a narrowly specified guarded architecture and emphasizes preregistration, paired inference, and deterministic-verifier endpoints. Key contrasts with some prior work that reports larger guarded-vs-baseline gains are: (a) shared_initial_candidate execution semantics (one initial sample shared across conditions), (b) a strict one-repair budget per intent, (c) a single tested model (gpt-5-mini), and (d) a synthetic verifier-capable task bank restricted to small topologies. These differences change the estimand and observable marginal benefit of a runtime guard and explain how previously reported larger gains can coexist with our bounded result [4],[7].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) and the analysis plan frozen before any model outputs were observed; the preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest. The design was paired_binary with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and an exact two-sided McNemar test for confirmatory inference. Key preregistered constraints included N=150 confirmatory intents, one initial model call per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics), and at most one guarded repair call per intent. Inclusion/exclusion and missingness rules, unit-tests for mapping and verifier coverage, and a power plan targeting a +15 percentage-point absolute improvement were preregistered.

Task generation and corpus. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by the preregistered generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) and span four intent families: reachability/isolation, ACL-like access changes, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, and uplink switchover patterns. Topologies were restricted to verifier-capable small networks (4–32 nodes). The generator produced difficulty labels (e.g., medium, hard, very_hard) that were archived per-task. Pre-execution mapping and verifier-coverage unit-tests were applied; no confirmatory exclusions occurred (exclusions = 0). Representative task manifests and seeds are archived, enabling deterministic reproduction of the corpus from the recorded generator seeds.

Model, adapter, and deterministic validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). The execution adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) enforced the one-initial/≤one-repair call budget per intent and implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a boolean pass/fail with normalized final-configuration text and diagnostics (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes).

Explicit runtime-sampling semantics (reviewer clarification). The archived execution model configuration (model_configuration.json) records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset). Concretely: no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced at generation time and therefore model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions. The model_configuration.json and per-call runtime metadata are archived for inspection; readers should consult these artifacts for exact recorded runtime metadata.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and inferential meaning (reviewer clarification). The execution contract used shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial model generation was produced and that identical sampled candidate was used to evaluate both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline could invoke at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. Consequently, the baseline success rate measures the validity of that single initial sampled candidate; the guarded vs baseline contrast therefore isolates the marginal effect of the single allowed repair applied to the identical candidate. This differs from independent-sampling designs where per-condition randomness can produce different estimands.

Execution accounting, retries, and contamination controls. Planned episodes = 300 (150 paired tasks × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 300; complete_pair_count = 150. The adapter recorded model_calls_used = 151 (150 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). Provider-call auditing in the deterministic reconciliation artifact reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}, and condition_counts = {shared: 150, guarded: 1}. Contamination checks reported zero flags and mapping unit-tests passed before batch execution. The preregistered missingness and retry policy (one deterministic retry after API timeout) was not invoked because there were no provider-call failures.

Scoring and primary analysis. Primary outcome: deterministic verifier pass/fail (binary). Primary analysis: exact two-sided McNemar on the paired contingency counts plus 95% bootstrap percentile confidence intervals computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis executor and code, paired contingency table, and condition summaries are archived and are the direct source of all numeric results presented below. Secondary contrasts and multiplicity corrections were preregistered but not used as confirmatory tests because the shared_initial_candidate enforcement constrained independent constrained-only draws.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 151 and artifact_hash_count = 1058. The deterministic reconciliation provider_call_audit lists hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 151, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 1}, and condition_counts: {shared: 150, guarded: 1}. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports no contamination flags.

Primary numerical outcomes and paired table. The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). The contingency table and condition summary are archived as analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics, revision iterations, and episode-level traces. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. That single repair converted one initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic validator. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces for each episode provide validation_before and validation_after states, normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and valid flag; representative traces are archived (execution/scoring/task-00000X-*.json). Example (task-000001): intent required a four-command safe shutdown-configure-restore sequence; shared-initial, baseline, and guarded responses all matched the reference normalized_configuration and the validator recorded parsed_command_count = 4 and valid = true.

Representative tasks and difficulty distribution. Representative task manifests archived in the bundle show a spectrum of difficulty: among six representative tasks included in the manuscript evidence three were labeled very_hard, two hard, and one medium. Despite this diversity the model's initial candidates achieved near-ceiling correctness on the frozen corpus. The deterministic generator seeds and reference answers allow deterministic reconstitution of the representative episodes.

Sensitivity and missingness checks. The preregistered sensitivity analysis treating missing guarded outputs as failures was not invoked because failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No exclusions or parse failures occurred. Contamination and mapping unit-tests passed prior to batch execution; analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains an empty flag set.

Quantitative interpretation. The observed marginal gain of ≈0.67 percentage points is numerically tiny and statistically non-significant under the preregistered test. Given the baseline's near-perfect pass rate the run experienced a ceiling effect that invalidated the preregistered power assumption (target detectable effect = 15 pp). The bootstrap CI upper bound (0.02) quantifies that, on this corpus and under the shared_initial_candidate semantics, any true marginal improvement of the guarded pipeline is small (<2 percentage points at the 95% CI level). These numeric facts are drawn directly from the archived analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and implications for preregistration. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline; baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 left almost no headroom for a +15 pp improvement. This outcome indicates that preregistered NetOps trials should include a short baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., a deterministic handful of tasks) to estimate baseline competence for the chosen model, prompt style, and generator difficulty and to adjust N or task difficulty accordingly. We recommend explicitly recording pilot-estimated baseline rates in preregistration to avoid overpowered or underpowered designs.

Semantics-driven estimand differences and operational meaning. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline measures the single initial sampled candidate while the guarded condition measures the marginal value of at most one repair applied to that same candidate. Independent-sampling designs or larger repair budgets answer different operational questions (average improvement over independent draws or cumulative repair resilience) and can produce larger observable gains when baseline sampling variance is higher. Practitioners should choose generation semantics and repair budgets to match the operational estimand they care about (marginal repair effect vs average outcome under repeated sampling or training).

Operational benefits beyond binary verification. Deterministic guarded workflows deliver operational affordances not captured solely by a binary pass/fail metric: auditable normalized configurations suitable for human review, standardized repair prompts that structure operator interaction, deterministic normalized outputs that support gating policies, and concise diagnostic traces (parsed_command_count, violation_codes) that accelerate triage. These secondary benefits can justify guarded architectures even when marginal verifier-pass improvements on a constrained corpus are small.

Threats to validity—summary. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally reduce sampling variance but limit condition-level randomness; adapter-enforced budgets and provider-audit artifacts mitigate cross-condition leakage (cross_condition_cache_reuse_observed = false). Construct validity: deterministic validator pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage; we mitigated mapping risk with unit-tests and archived mapping artifacts, but residual risks remain. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic tasks constrained to small topologies limit production inference. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumptions were invalidated by an unexpectedly high baseline; reported p-values and CI are presented without overinterpretation.

Practical recommendations and next-step designs. From the preregistered artifacts we recommend: (1) run a short baseline-calibration pilot before fixing N; (2) state generation semantics explicitly (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) in preregistration; (3) preregister repair-budget sensitivity analyses; (4) archive mapping/verifier unit-tests and run them prior to batch runs to prevent post-hoc exclusions; and (5) include provider-call audits (model_calls_used, stage_counts, cache_miss/hit) in reporting to document execution budgets and stage-level behavior. Future experiments that address external validity should evaluate independent per-condition sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, multiple model families, and scaling to larger topologies with expanded verifier coverage.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single deterministic verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased the verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
